{{Short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox college sports team season |year = 2022–23 |team = Kansas Jayhawks |sport = Basketball |image = 2022–23 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team.jpg |image_size = 295 |conference = Big 12 Conference |division = |short_conf = Big 12 |CoachRank = 11 |APRank = 4 |record = 28–8 |conf_record = 13–5 |head_coach = [[Bill Self]] |hc_year = 20th |hc_games = suspended first 4 games, illness for Big 12 Tournament and NCAA Tournament |head_coach2 = [[Norm Roberts]] |hc_games2 = acting, 4–0 |asst_coach1 = [[Jeremy Case]] |ac1_year = 2nd |asst_coach2 = Norm Roberts |ac2_year = 12th |asst_coach3 = [[Kurtis Townsend]] |ac3_year = 19th |stadium = [[Allen Fieldhouse]] |champion =[[2022–23 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|Big 12 regular season]] champions |tourney= [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result= Second Round }} {{2022–23 Big 12 men's basketball standings}} The '''2022–23 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Kansas]] in the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], which was the Jayhawks' 125th basketball season. The Jayhawks, members of the [[Big 12 Conference]], played their home games at [[Allen Fieldhouse]] in [[Lawrence, Kansas]]. They were led by 20th year [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] head coach [[Bill Self]]. Kansas finished first in the Big 12 in the regular season. The Jayhawks qualified for the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] but lost in the 2nd round. ==Season summary== On November 2, 2022, Kansas announced that Self and assistant coach [[Kurtis Townsend]] would serve a four-game suspension for alleged recruiting violations from a [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal|2017 FBI probe]]. Assistant coach [[Norm Roberts]] served as acting head coach during the suspension.{{cite web |title=Kansas suspends Bill Self for 4 games in infractions case |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/34932400/kansas-suspends-bill-self-4-games-infractions-case |website=ESPN.com}} Roberts would serve as acting head again during the Big 12 and NCAA Tournaments while Self was out following a procedure on his heart.{{cite news |title=KU's Self misses loss to Arkansas amid recovery |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35887977/kansas-bill-self-coach-2nd-round-game-vs-arkansas |work=ESPN.com |date=March 18, 2023 |language=en}} In January, the Jayhawks lost to Kansas State, TCU, and Baylor for what is only their 4th 3 game losing streak under Self, and only the 11th losing streak of any length. Kansas finished the regular season 25–6, their 33rd consecutive 20+ win season and their 38th in the previous 39 seasons. After defeating Texas Tech on February 28, the Jayhawks clinched the Big 12 title, their 21st regular season Big 12 title and their 64th regular season conference title. All of the Jayhawks 6 regular season losses came to ranked teams and five of the six finished the season ranked in the AP and all six made the NCAA tournament. In turn, the Jayhawks were undefeated against unranked teams. They also went undefeated against quadrant 2, 3, and 4 teams with a combined 10–0 record in those quads. They also finished the season with 17 quadrant 1 wins, the most in the nation.{{cite web |title=Most Quadrant 1 Wins for the 2023 NCAA Tournament (March 12) |url=https://sports.betmgm.com/en/blog/college-basketball-ncaa-tournament-quadrant-1-wins/ |website=BetMGM.com}} Redshirt junior forward [[Jalen Wilson]] was named First Team All-American by the AP.{{cite web |title=The Associated Press 2022-23 Men’s All-America Team |url=https://apnews.com/article/ap-all-america-mens-basketball-team-2ab037abcde5157ad840f7dcd22cc8a4 |website=APNews.com}} The Jayhawks qualified for the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] with an at-large bid. It was the Jayhawks NCAA record extending 33rd consecutive and their 51st in program history. They won their first round game over Howard 96–68, extending their first round winning streak to 16 straight. They would lose in the second round to Arkansas 72–71 marking the third time in their last four tournament appearances they failed to make the Sweet 16. ==Offseason== ===Players graduated=== Below are players who ran out of eligibility or seniors that did not declare intent for a 5th year as allowed by the NCAA due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. {| class="wikitable" !
